chosen.premise: Omanyte fossils preserve bite marks from Archeops, revealing that this ancient shell Pokémon was prey.
chosen.hook: Omanyte fossils carry evidence of who hunted them.
chosen.visualIdea: Zoom into fossil shell bite marks, then reveal Archeops as the likely prehistoric predator.
chosen.note: Fossil bite marks provide a sharp mystery, a named predator, and an immediately visual reveal. The premise is strongly backed, but by only one entry.

candidates.premise: Omanyte uses air stored in its shell as built-in ballast, controlling whether it sinks or rises.
candidates.hook: Omanyte’s shell is also a built-in dive tank.
candidates.visualIdea: Show shell air expanding to lift Omanyte and compressing to send it downward.
candidates.note: An unusually concrete and memorable biological mechanic, with excellent visual potential; support rests on only one Pokédex entry.

candidates.premise: Omanyte navigates and swims by twisting all 10 tentacles, making its movement look like drifting.
candidates.hook: Omanyte doesn’t swim like a fish—it twists ten tentacles.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate ten tentacles twisting in sequence as Omanyte glides through an ancient sea.
candidates.note: The ten-tentacle swimming mechanism is highly specific to Omanyte and strongly supported by multiple entries, but it is less surprising to knowledgeable fans.

candidates.premise: Omanyte is an extinct fossil Pokémon that can be restored—but escaped or released individuals are now causing problems.
candidates.hook: Omanyte came back from extinction… and became a problem.
candidates.visualIdea: Transform a fossil into living Omanyte, then fill the modern waterway with escaped specimens.
candidates.note: The contrast between extinction and becoming a modern ecological problem is compelling, though the invasive-problem claim is supported by only one entry and lacks detail.

candidates.premise: Omanyte’s fossil-restored life has a fixed next step: reaching level 40 turns it into Omastar.
candidates.hook: Omanyte’s ancient comeback has a level-40 deadline.
candidates.visualIdea: As a restored Omanyte gains levels, stop at 40 and reveal the larger Omastar transformation.
candidates.note: The level-40 evolution creates a clean visual structure, but it is mainly a standard game mechanic rather than a distinctive piece of Omanyte lore.

candidates.premise: When attacked, Omanyte’s survival rule is simple: withdraw completely inside its hard shell.
candidates.hook: Omanyte’s entire defense is disappearing into its shell.
candidates.visualIdea: Show an attacker approach as Omanyte rapidly retracts until only its hard shell remains.
candidates.note: The defense rule is clear and well supported, but retreating into a shell is common among shell-based Pokémon and offers limited new information.

rounds.request: The strongest angles are already viable; a still stronger version would add corroborating fossil or species-history evidence explaining how the bite marks identify Archeops, while preserving the single concrete mystery.
